dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: #I'm here, {NICKNAME}!

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Do you have a new story for me? I'll trade you some Candied Ajilenakh Nuts — I made them myself.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: How do you like it here?

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: I think the answer to that should be pretty obvious.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: You should be able to tell from just one look, like when you peer into a crystal-clear lake and you can see all the fish swimming around inside of it.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: It's very pleasant here. Even the wind brushing against my toes feels soft and gentle. So of course, I love it.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Glad to hear it.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: As much as a little bird might love exploring the forests and mountains, tasting new and different fruits every day...

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: ...After a long flight, it still needs a place to land and rest its weary wings.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: So I'm glad that I can roost here in your nest for a while.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Also, it's much more spacious here than a birdcage.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Stay as long as you like, Nahida.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Thank you for being so kind. I know that you mean it, and I'll make the most of my stay here.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Would you like to have a chat with me?

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Sure, but instead of diving into story time, let's talk about what's troubling you.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: I'm sure you're wondering how I knew.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Well, your troubles are written on your face, silly! I'm always observing you, you know.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: You look as miserable as a Lavender Melon that's been struck by lightning.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I feel like nothing's been going my way lately...

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Don't lose heart. Sometimes you might feel like you're the unluckiest person in the world, but for all you know, it could also just be an unfortunate situation.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Well, to use an analogy... Let's say a Rishboland Tiger ate a fox and got diarrhea.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: You can't know for sure whether the diarrhea was caused by eating the fox or by something inside the fox's stomach. Does that make sense?

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: If Rishboland Tigers stopped eating foxes out of fear of diarrhea, they would have become extinct a long time ago.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: As long as the Rishboland Tiger keeps eating foxes, and as long as we keep living our lives, we'll experience all kinds of different situations. Fortunate, unfortunate, and everything in between.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: There, there. You're doing great. Have a headpat.

choices.text: Can you whip out one of your analogies?

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Hmm... Well, let's say a Rishboland Tiger ate a fox and got diarrhea.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Anything you want to do?

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: #May I start with a question, {NICKNAME}? Do you really enjoy collecting things?

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Sometimes you remind me of a Sumpter Beast, plodding along with a big pack full of materials and supplies.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: I'm quite curious. You already have more than enough resources to last a lifetime, so why do you keep bringing everything with you?

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: And why do you still collect even more during your travels?

choices.text: You're right. It's because I enjoy it.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Mm, yes, I thought so. Okay, that makes sense.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: People do sometimes act irrationally for the sake of pursuing their interests.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Just like the Forest Boar that fell in love with a Shroom-Kin. It changed its own form just to ensure the Shroom-Kin's survival.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: In the end, they were eaten together as a delicacy... Um, but that's besides the point.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: I don't feel one way or another about collecting, but since it's something you enjoy, I'd like to join in and see what it's like.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: I want to travel across this vast land with you, experience everything you enjoy, and do all the things you do.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Will you indulge my curiosity... and will you accept my request?

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Then let's face the sun and pick the first Mint we find.

choices.text: I'd say it's more of a habit than a hobby.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: A habit? Oh, I see.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: So what about forging weapons, cooking, and making Condensed Resin? They're useful behaviors that benefit you. Is that why they've turned into habits as well?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: That sounds about right.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: So what about... making lots of friends, helping them solve their problems, and reading their letters from front to back? Are those habits, too?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Well, not exactly...

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Don't worry, I'm not trying to pry, and I wouldn't let something like that affect what I think of you.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: I know there are definitely good reasons for your behavior. I'm only asking out of curiosity.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Since you are also driven by emotions, maybe you can understand my thoughts right now.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Morning, Nahida.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Today's sunrise is the same splendid color as the breast feathers of a Dusk Bird.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: I'm really curious to find out what the first thing you'll do today is.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Good night, Nahida.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: #Good night, {NICKNAME}.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Why don't you take a final trip to the bathroom before bed?

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: It'll improve the quality of your sleep. Seems like very helpful advice, so are you gonna take it?

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: It's peaceful here, like... a leaf floating in the middle of a perfectly still pond...

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Let me be a little firefly taking a rest on that leaf. When night falls, all the stars in the sky will adorn your dreams.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: I hope you have sweet dreams tonight.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: I see, so you've combined all your favorite sights from your travels into one.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Like picking all your favorite candies out from a huge pile, and building your dream house with them.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Um, do you mind if I come in from the chimney, just to take a look?
